Identifier and Mapping Information Schema Source from schema: https://w3id.org/htan/acquisition_method_type_enum LinkML Source name : AcquisitionMethodTypeEnum title : acquisition_method_type from_schema : https://w3id.org/htan/acquisition_method_type_enum permissible_values : Autopsy : text : Autopsy description : Autopsy; an examination and dissection of a dead body to determine cause of death or the changes produced by disease. Biopsy : text : Biopsy description : The removal of tissue specimens or fluid from the living body for microscopic examination, performed to establish a diagnosis. Blood draw : text : Blood draw description : A small volume of blood removed for testing or storage. Core needle biopsy : text : Core needle biopsy description : The removal of a tissue sample using a needle with a relatively large diameter, for microscopic examination. Excisional Biopsy : text : Excisional Biopsy description : A surgical procedure in which an entire lesion is removed for microscopic examination. Fine needle aspirate : text : Fine needle aspirate description : The removal of tissue or fluid with a thin needle for examination under a microscope. Forceps Biopsy : text : Forceps Biopsy description : The removal of a tissue sample using a specially-designed endoscope consisting of a slender flexible forceps with movable cup-shaped jaws. The jaws are closed around the tissue to be collected and while closed the forceps are withdrawn to capture the biopsy tissue. Incisional Biopsy : text : Incisional Biopsy description : A surgical procedure in which part of a lesion is removed for microscopic examination. Lymphadenectomy (regional nodes) : text : Lymphadenectomy (regional nodes) description : 'Surgical removal of lymph nodes, usually done to assess the spread of cancer: A lymph node that drains lymph from a region of interest.' Not applicable : text : Not applicable description : Determination of a value is not relevant in the current context. Not reported : text : Not reported description : Not provided or available. Not specified : text : Not specified description : Not stated explicitly or in detail. Other : text : Other description : Different than the one(s) previously specified or mentioned. Pancreaticoduodenectomy : text : Pancreaticoduodenectomy description : Surgical excision of all or part of the pancreas and duodenum. Punch biopsy : text : Punch biopsy description : Removal of a disk of skin tissue, for microscopic examination, using a punch. Re-excision : text : Re-excision description : A surgical procedure to remove the remaining abnormal tissues from the body, not completely removed in an earlier attempt. Sentinel node biopsy : text : Sentinel node biopsy description : Surgical removal and examination of the sentinel node, the lymph node which is first in receiving the lymphatic drainage of a specified anatomic location and is most likely to be affected by the lymphatic spread of cancer. Shave biopsy : text : Shave biopsy description : Removal skin tissue, for microscopic examination, using a blade oriented in the horizontal plane of the skin surface. Surgical Resection : text : Surgical Resection description : The surgical removal of a lesion, often as part of a biopsy and with healthy margins. Unknown : text : Unknown description : Not known, not observed, not recorded, or refused.

docs.text: name : AcquisitionMethodTypeEnum title : acquisition_method_type from_schema : https://w3id.org/htan/acquisition_method_type_enum permissible_values : Autopsy : text : Autopsy description : Autopsy; an examination and dissection of a dead body to determine cause of death or the changes produced by disease. Biopsy : text : Biopsy description : The removal of tissue specimens or fluid from the living body for microscopic examination, performed to establish a diagnosis. Blood draw : text : Blood draw description : A small volume of blood removed for testing or storage. Core needle biopsy : text : Core needle biopsy description : The removal of a tissue sample using a needle with a relatively large diameter, for microscopic examination. Excisional Biopsy : text : Excisional Biopsy description : A surgical procedure in which an entire lesion is removed for microscopic examination. Fine needle aspirate : text : Fine needle aspirate description : The removal of tissue or fluid with a thin needle for examination under a microscope. Forceps Biopsy : text : Forceps Biopsy description : The removal of a tissue sample using a specially-designed endoscope consisting of a slender flexible forceps with movable cup-shaped jaws. The jaws are closed around the tissue to be collected and while closed the forceps are withdrawn to capture the biopsy tissue. Incisional Biopsy : text : Incisional Biopsy description : A surgical procedure in which part of a lesion is removed for microscopic examination. Lymphadenectomy (regional nodes) : text : Lymphadenectomy (regional nodes) description : 'Surgical removal of lymph nodes, usually done to assess the spread of cancer: A lymph node that drains lymph from a region of interest.' Not applicable : text : Not applicable description : Determination of a value is not relevant in the current context. Not reported : text : Not reported description : Not provided or available. Not specified : text : Not specified description : Not stated explicitly or in detail. Other : text : Other description : Different than the one(s) previously specified or mentioned. Pancreaticoduodenectomy : text : Pancreaticoduodenectomy description : Surgical excision of all or part of the pancreas and duodenum. Punch biopsy : text : Punch biopsy description : Removal of a disk of skin tissue, for microscopic examination, using a punch. Re-excision : text : Re-excision description : A surgical procedure to remove the remaining abnormal tissues from the body, not completely removed in an earlier attempt. Sentinel node biopsy : text : Sentinel node biopsy description : Surgical removal and examination of the sentinel node, the lymph node which is first in receiving the lymphatic drainage of a specified anatomic location and is most likely to be affected by the lymphatic spread of cancer. Shave biopsy : text : Shave biopsy description : Removal skin tissue, for microscopic examination, using a blade oriented in the horizontal plane of the skin surface. Surgical Resection : text : Surgical Resection description : The surgical removal of a lesion, often as part of a biopsy and with healthy margins. Unknown : text : Unknown description : Not known, not observed, not recorded, or refused.

It consists of the epidermis, dermis, and skin appendages. meaning : NCIT:C12443 Sputum : text : Sputum description : Material containing mucus, cellular debris, microorganisms and sometimes blood or pus. It is ejected through the mouth from the lungs, bronchi, and trachea. meaning : NCIT:C12444 Stool : text : Stool description : The material discharged from the bowel during defecation. It consists of undigested food, intestinal mucus, epithelial cells, and bacteria. meaning : NCIT:C12437 Tissue : text : Tissue description : An anatomical structure consisting of similarly specialized cells and intercellular matrix, aggregated according to genetically determined spatial relationships, performing a specific function. meaning : NCIT:C12433 Unknown : text : Unknown description : Not known, observed, recorded; or reported as unknown by the data contributor. meaning : NCIT:C17998 Urine : text : Urine description : The fluid that is excreted by the kidneys. It is stored in the bladder and discharged through the urethra. meaning : NCIT:C12437 Xenograft : text : Xenograft description : The transfer of cells, tissues, or organs from a donor into a recipient of another species. meaning : NCIT:C12445

Although this term may be used to describe any therapy involving the use of chemical-based agents, it is most commonly used to refer to the variety of chemical-based agents employed to treat cancer. Cancer chemotherapy works by arresting or killing the growth and spread of cancer cells. Because cancer cells usually divide much faster than normal cells, they are often very sensitive to the inhibitory actions of chemotherapeutic agents. Chemotherapy may also include agents that enhance immune function or alter hormonal activity. Although this term may be used to describe any therapy involving the use of chemical-based agents, it is most commonly used to refer to the variety of chemical-based agents employed to treat cancer. Cancer chemotherapy works by arresting or killing the growth and spread of cancer cells. Because cancer cells usually divide much faster than normal cells, they are often very sensitive to the inhibitory actions of chemotherapeutic agents. Chemotherapy may also include agents that enhance immune function or alter hormonal activity.
